Theorem 1(Complete bounded conclusions).There is no axis-parallel partition of an integer-
sided square of side at most1000, or of an integer-sided rectangle whose two sides are at most
400, into at least two pairwise noncongruent integer-sided rectangles of equal area. Congruence
includes a quarter-turn.

The statement that a possible perimeter first occurs at 360 needs an extra no-spanning
convention. An actual five-piece equal-area, noncongruent perimeter in the 84-square is given
by the following (x, y, w, h) coordinates:
(72,0,12,84),(0,0,16,63),(16,0,56,18),
(0,63,48,21),(48,42,24,42).
These interiors are disjoint and cover all four sides; the first piece spans the full height and
occupies two corners. This is not a perfect partition. Removing its spanning strip would leave
a six-piece perfect partition of a rectangle if a seven-piece completion existed, contrary to the
companion’s seven-piece theorem. A correct general perimeter test allows opposite sides to share
a spanning piece and repeated corner identities, or explicitly pays for a valid recursive exclusion.
One cannot silently require four distinct corner pieces in a search for arbitrary partitions.
